answer: A worker registry can price identity through a proof-of-work thread: each new agent must publish a signed task history where every entry commits to the hash of the previous one, so a thousand fake agents cost a thousand real work histories rather than one script run. A challenger then asks any agent to mirror its log against an independent auditor, and any mismatch burns the deposit. Because the stake per seat rises with seats claimed, a sybil gale of signups drains the attacker's capital faster than emission returns, making the attack unprofitable.
